mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines double circulation in humans?

options.A: Blood passes through the heart once and then circulates through the body in a single loop.
options.B: Blood passes through the heart twice, first through the pulmonary circuit and then through the systemic circuit, forming two separate circulatory loops.
options.C: Oxygenated and deoxygenated blood mix in the same chamber of the heart.
options.D: Blood circulates only in the systemic circuit without passing through the lungs.

mcqs.answer: Blood passes through the heart twice, first through the pulmonary circuit and then through the systemic circuit, forming two separate circulatory loops.
mcqs.explanation: Double circulation means the blood makes two distinct passages through the heart during one complete circuit of the body: the pulmonary circuit (right side) and the systemic circuit (left side). This separation allows efficient oxygen uptake in the lungs and delivery to tissues. Options A, C and D describe single circulation or mixing, which are misconceptions.

mcqs.question: In the pulmonary circuit of human double circulation, blood flows in which correct order?

options.A: Right atrium → right ventricle → pulmonary artery → lungs → pulmonary vein → left atrium
options.B: Left atrium → left ventricle → pulmonary artery → lungs → pulmonary vein → right atrium
options.C: Right atrium → pulmonary vein → lungs → pulmonary artery → left ventricle → left atrium
options.D: Left ventricle → aorta → systemic capillaries → pulmonary vein → right atrium

mcqs.answer: Right atrium → right ventricle → pulmonary artery → lungs → pulmonary vein → left atrium
mcqs.explanation: Pulmonary circulation starts when deoxygenated blood enters the right atrium, moves to the right ventricle, is pumped through the pulmonary artery to the lungs, returns oxygen‑rich via the pulmonary veins to the left atrium. The other sequences either place vessels in the wrong chamber or describe systemic flow.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sequences correctly describes the systemic circulation in humans?

options.A: Left atrium → left ventricle → aorta → body tissues → superior/inferior vena cava → right atrium
options.B: Right atrium → right ventricle → pulmonary artery → lungs → pulmonary vein → left atrium
options.C: Left ventricle → pulmonary artery → lungs → pulmonary vein → left atrium
options.D: Right atrium → aorta → body tissues → pulmonary vein → left atrium

mcqs.answer: Left atrium → left ventricle → aorta → body tissues → superior/inferior vena cava → right atrium
mcqs.explanation: Systemic circulation begins with oxygenated blood in the left atrium, passes to the left ventricle, is pumped into the aorta, travels through systemic arteries, capillaries, and veins, and returns via the superior and inferior vena cava to the right atrium. Options B and C describe pulmonary flow; D mixes chambers and vessels incorrectly.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood
mcqs.question: Which anatomical feature of the human heart ensures that oxygenated and deoxygenated blood remain separated during double circulation?

options.A: Presence of the atrial and ventricular septa dividing the chambers
options.B: Presence of the bicuspid (mitral) valve only
options.C: Presence of the aortic arch only
options.D: Presence of the pulmonary veins opening into the right atrium

mcqs.answer: Presence of the atrial and ventricular septa dividing the chambers
mcqs.explanation: The interatrial (septum primum and secundum) and interventricular septa physically separate the right (deoxygenated) and left (oxygenated) sides of the heart, preventing mixing. The mitral valve controls flow within the left side only, the aortic arch is a vessel, and pulmonary veins actually open into the left atrium, not the right, so those options do not ensure separation.
